messages:
maria: Heads up — spotted a raw service token in logs for prod/indexer talking to Redis. snippet below from the ELK ingest, timestamp 2026-03-21T14:02:10Z

maria: ```
WARN 2026-03-21T14:02:10Z indexer.redis Connecting to cache host=redis-prod-1 token=sk_live_01f4b2e9c0a7...
```

sam: Wow, that looks like a full long-lived token. Is this coming from the repo or runtime?

maria: runtime. The app is reading from Vault KV v2 but the token shows up in a debug log from the redis client. Likely someone left debug logging on in the indexer container.

security-bot: Incident classifier: "credentials-exposure"; severity: medium -> escalate to oncall if blast radius unknown.

ben: @devops-oncall I've started a read-only search across ELK for that token prefix and related service IDs. Early results: same token appears in 11 log lines across prod-us-east and prod-us-west over the last 48h.

maria: Confirmed token is stored at Vault path `secret/data/redis/indexer` (KV v2). The entry is a static token, not an AppRole ephemeral token. It's wrapped by our KMS but the value itself is plaintext once read by the app.

sam: Proposed containment steps (short): 1) Revoke the token immediately in Redis ACLs. 2) Create a rotated token in Vault (new version) and update deployments. 3) Sweep logs and partner systems for leakage. 4) Hardening: remove debug logging, switch to short-lived creds (Vault dynamic credentials or AWS IAM).

ben: On it. I'll: - remove the leaked token from Redis ACLs, - create a new token in Vault as a new KV version, - gate rollout behind a canary. ETA 20m.

devops-oncall: Before revocation: which services use this token? If we cut it we may break indexer and downstream pipelines. maria, can you list processes?

maria: indexer-prod (k8s Deployment indexer-v2), a small ingestion job (ingest-worker), and a partner shim (partner-sync) that runs in prod-west. Blast radius small but user-visible.

ben: I'll rotate gracefully: create new token, patch k8s secret, roll indexer canary (1 pod), verify, then full rollout. Command I'll run: ```bash
# create new token (Redis)
redis-cli ACL SETUSER indexer_rotated on >legacy >allcommands ~* +@all
# put into Vault KV v2
vault kv put secret/redis/indexer token="<new-token>"
```

sam: For Vault best practice: don't delete old version — create version n+1 and mark previous as deprecated. We also need to update KMS wrapping policy if we rotate the KMS key. Are we rotating KMS too?

maria: Not required now. KMS protects at-rest; the problem is app-level debug logs. KMS rotation is a separate follow-up. For now focus on token rotation and log purge.

security-bot: Action item created: SEC-4283 "Prod Redis token log leak — rotate and audit" assigned to ben, priority P1.

devops-oncall: I'll also run a Vault audit for access to `secret/redis/indexer` to see who read the token. Command: `vault audit list && vault read sys/audit` then grep for that path.

ben: Quick checklist I'm executing now: - [x] create rotated token in Redis - [x] put new token into Vault (kv v2 new version) - [ ] patch k8s Secret `indexer-redis` using new value - [ ] roll canary - [ ] verify metrics (errors, rate) - [ ] full rollout - [ ] purge logs containing token (ELK keep policy + delete) - [ ] postmortem and follow-up on debug logging

maria: On log purge: we can ask platform-logging to remove specific log entries and set an exclusion rule to stop forwarding debug logs from indexer. @ben please include the time ranges.

ben: Noted. I'll add exact timestamps and request deletion ticket after canary succeeds.

sam: Long term follow-ups (for postmortem): - switch indexer to Vault dynamic creds (if Redis supports role-based ephemeral tokens) or short-lived tokens with TTL enforced, - add logging middleware to redact secrets, - add CI check to fail builds if debug env var is true in prod images.

devops-oncall: One more: update RBAC so only the service account `indexer-svc` can read this secret path. Right now there are 3 team identities with read access. I'll tighten policy and do an access re-review.

maria: Good. Also add an alert to Console for any future token-like patterns in logs (regex match) and set to page security on first occurrence.

security-bot: Incident state -> contained (revoked token + canary verified). Next: postmortem + compliance ticket for audit trail.

ben: Canary passed. Rolling full. Will follow up with CF for log purge ticket ID when created.

maria: Thanks all. Postmortem draft incoming, will include timeline, root cause (debug logging), and specific remediation (rotate -> use dynamic creds -> RBAC tighten -> KMS rotation plan deferred). :lock: :page_facing_up:
